items.headline: 今天，旅行者 1 号将距地球一光日
items.summary: NASA 预计，北京时间 11 月 18 日 18:16 左右，旅行者 1 号将距地球约 259 亿公里。一光日是光走 24 小时的距离。在这里，无线电指令约一天才能抵达；即使探测器立即回复，地球也要约两天才能收到回信。
items.summary_en: NASA expects Voyager 1 to be about 25.9 billion kilometres from Earth at around 18:16 Beijing time on 18 November. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours. A radio command takes about a day to arrive; even an immediate reply would reach Earth about two days after the command was sent.

items.headline: 冀东一块 39.5 亿年前的岩石，记录了什么？
items.headline_en: What Does a 3.95-Billion-Year-Old Rock Tell Us?
items.summary: 11 月 11 日，《自然》发表了对冀东一块古老片麻岩的研究。研究者用锆石测定岩石年龄，又从岩石成分推断，形成它的岩浆来自曾在地表附近被改造、后来沉入深处的玄武质地壳。这可能是早期地球曾短暂发生俯冲的线索。
items.summary_en: On 11 November, Nature published a study of ancient gneiss from eastern Hebei. Researchers used zircon to date the rock. Its chemistry suggests that the magma came from basaltic crust altered near the surface and later buried deep underground. This may be evidence of a brief episode of subduction on early Earth.

items.headline: 一块深海结核里，藏着 245 只小动物
items.headline_en: 245 Tiny Animals in One Deep-Sea Nodule
items.summary: 11 月 11 日发表的研究检查了太平洋深海的 244 块富金属结核，平均每块发现 17 只小动物，最多的一块有 245 只。结核里的细小裂缝给不足一毫米的动物提供了栖身处。开采这些结核，带走的不只是矿石，还有它们的栖息地。
items.summary_en: A study published on 11 November examined 244 metal-rich nodules from the deep Pacific. They contained an average of 17 tiny animals, with 245 in the most crowded one. Cracks inside the nodules give animals smaller than a millimetre a place to live. Mining the nodules would remove their habitat along with the minerals.

items.headline: 一颗小行星为何有一道赤道山脊？
items.headline_en: Why Does an Asteroid Have an Equatorial Ridge?
items.summary: 11 月 12 日，欧洲航天局公开赫拉探测器从 56 公里外拍到的照片：直径约 780 米的迪迪莫斯小行星有一道明显的赤道山脊。它每 2.2 小时自转一圈。模型显示，快速自转可能让表面的松散物质从较高纬度滑向赤道，在那里堆积。
items.summary_en: On 12 November, ESA released a photograph taken by Hera from 56 kilometres away. Didymos, an asteroid about 780 metres across, has a distinct equatorial ridge and rotates once every 2.2 hours. Models suggest rapid rotation may drive loose material from higher latitudes towards the equator, where it can build up.

items.headline: 隔着云，卫星怎样追踪熔岩？
items.headline_en: How Can Satellites Track Lava Through Clouds?
items.summary: 11 月 7 日发表的研究重新分析了夏威夷基拉韦厄火山的卫星雷达记录。雷达发出微波，夜间或有云时也能接收回波；地表的粗糙程度和坡度会改变回波强弱。比较不同时刻的影像，可以画出熔岩扩展的范围，并估算火山口深度的变化。
items.summary_en: A study published on 7 November re-examined satellite radar records of Hawai‘i’s Kīlauea volcano. Radar sends out microwaves and can receive echoes at night and through clouds. Surface roughness and slope affect the strength of those echoes. Comparing images over time can map spreading lava and estimate changes in crater depth.

items.headline: 海洋热浪也能下潜到 150 米
items.headline_en: Marine Heatwaves Can Reach 150 Metres Deep
items.summary: 11 月 10 日发表的研究分析了 31 年的海洋资料。在珊瑚礁海域，越往深处，热浪天数通常越少，但热浪的累积强度可能更高。强厄尔尼诺或持续多年的拉尼娜期间，强热浪曾延伸到约 150 米深。只看海面温度，可能低估珊瑚礁承受的热压力。
items.summary_en: A study published on 10 November analysed 31 years of ocean data. In coral reef regions, deeper waters typically see fewer heatwave days, but deep heatwaves can have greater cumulative intensity. During strong El Niño or multi-year La Niña events, severe heatwaves reached about 150 metres down. Surface temperatures alone can miss some of the heat stress on reefs.

previous_answers.headline: 选一个三位数，要求百位与个位相差至少2。把它的数字顺序倒过来，用较大的数减去较小的数。再把所得差的数字顺序倒过来，将这两个数相加。不必知道最初选的数，你能预测最后的结果吗？说明理由。（倒序后开头的0可以略去。）
previous_answers.headline_en: Choose a three-digit number whose first and last digits differ by at least 2. Reverse its digits, then subtract the smaller number from the larger. Reverse the digits of the difference and add these two numbers. Can you predict the final total without knowing the starting number? Explain why. Any leading zero in a reversed number may be omitted.
previous_answers.explanation: 设首尾数字之差为 d，则减出的数是 99d，三位数字依次为 d−1、9、10−d。倒序相加时，两端各凑成 9，中间相加得 18；进位后就是 1089。
previous_answers.explanation_en: Let d be the difference between the first and last digits. Subtracting gives 99d, whose digits are d−1, 9 and 10−d. Adding its reversal gives 9 at both ends and 18 in the middle before carrying, which gives 1,089.
previous_answers.subject: W46 · 倒序数之谜解答

previous_answers.headline: 12张卡片分别写着1至12。充分洗匀后，随机抽出3张，不放回。三张卡片上的数之和能被3整除的概率是多少？请用清楚的分类计数说明答案，而不是只靠模拟。
previous_answers.headline_en: Twelve cards are numbered 1 to 12. Shuffle them thoroughly and draw three without replacement. What is the probability that their sum is divisible by 3? Explain your answer by counting cases, rather than relying only on a simulation.
previous_answers.explanation: 按除以 3 的余数分三类，每类 4 张。要使和整除，三张的余数要么全相同，要么各不相同。符合的组合有 3×4＋4³＝76 种；一共 220 种，所以是 76/220＝19/55。
previous_answers.explanation_en: There are four cards in each remainder class modulo 3. For the sum to be divisible by 3, the remainders must be all equal or all different. This gives 3×4 + 4³ = 76 valid triples out of 220, so the probability is 19/55.
previous_answers.subject: W46 · 余数与概率解答

previous_answers.headline: 7名选手进行单循环比赛：每两人恰好比赛一场，每场都有一名胜者，没有平局。证明：无论比赛结果如何，总能把7人排成一列，使每个人都赢过紧挨在自己后面的人。注意：不要求一个人赢过自己后面的所有人。
previous_answers.headline_en: Seven players compete in a round-robin tournament: every pair plays exactly once, and every match has one winner, with no draws. Prove that, whatever the results, the players can always be arranged in a line so that each player beat the person immediately after them. A player need not have beaten everyone farther down the line.
previous_answers.explanation: 先排一人，再逐个加入。新选手若谁也没赢过，就放在末尾；否则把他插到队中第一位被他打败的人前面。若前面还有一人，那人一定赢过新选手，所以两个新的相邻关系都成立。
previous_answers.explanation_en: Start with one player and add the rest one at a time. If the newcomer beat nobody in the line, put them at the end. Otherwise, insert them just before the first player they beat. Any player immediately before that position must have beaten the newcomer, so both new links work.
previous_answers.subject: W46 · 胜者队列解答

challenges.headline_en: Three opaque boxes contain two red balls, two blue balls, and one of each, respectively. The three labels, “two red”, “two blue” and “one of each”, are all wrong. You may choose one box and draw one ball without looking inside. How can you identify the contents of all three boxes?
